# Run ledger — P26.14 (federal procurement depth: USAspending award sweep + widened SAM.gov)

## Spec / Base / Branch / Config

- **Spec:** `docs/tickets/P26.14__federal-procurement-depth.md` (FEDERAL.1) —
  federal awards are a higher-signal procurement layer than municipal records:
  ALPR, drones, cell-site simulators, acoustic gunshot detection, predictive
  analytics, and camera systems are often purchased through federal agencies or
  pass-through grants. Scope: complete the `usaspending` connector over the
  public award-search API (POST `/api/v2/search/spending_by_award/`, no key),
  widen the keyed `sam_gov` sweep to the same surveillance keyword space, emit
  typed `procurement_notice` claims (award/notice id, recipient, awarding
  agency, amount, period, description, matched keyword), keep verbatim
  literals + locators, and preserve **procured ≠ deployed** semantics.
- **Branch:** `devin/p26-14-federal-procurement` — stacked on
  `devin/p26-13-catalog-sweep` (PR #105). Head at hosted run: `67b8b81`.
- **Date:** 2026-09-18. Same GCP posture as P26.8–P26.13: user account
  `14stevevitali@gmail.com` on `zeta-medley-508121-u7`; per-job upserts
  (`gcloud run jobs update`), never `scheduled-ops.sh --apply` (host ADC file
  corrupt, as recorded). Local Docker unresponsive again — the hosted image
  was built with **Cloud Build** (`ops/Dockerfile`, repo-root context).

## What landed

### 1. Sweep plans as data — `procurement_vocab.toml` (+~95 lines)

- `[usaspending_sweep]` — 19 reviewed surveillance keywords (license-plate
  family, facial recognition, drone/UAS, cell-site simulator/stingray,
  shotspotter/acoustic gunshot, surveillance/video cameras, predictive
  policing, geofence, data broker, gunshot detection, RTCC, body camera) and
  three reviewed awarding agencies (Department of Justice, Department of
  Homeland Security, Department of Defense — the pass-through funder set).
  `[usaspending_sweep.bounds]`: page_size 100, sub-award slices ≤ 2 pages,
  prime slices ≤ 1 page, agency slices 1 page, 2018-01-01→2026-12-31 window,
  assistance award-type codes (02–11) for sub slices and all types (A–D +
  02–11) for prime slices, and the API display-label field lists.
- `[sam_gov_sweep]` — the same 19 keywords, limit 25, posted 2026 window.
- `predicate_allowlist` +`description` +`matched_keyword`; `vocab_version`
  → `2026.09.18-p26.14`.

### 2. Connector — `procurement.py` (+~430 lines)

- `usaspending_award_targets()` generates **60 bounded POST targets**:
  19 sub-award keyword slices × 2 pages (38), 19 prime-award keyword
  slices × 1 page (19), 3 awarding-agency slices × 1 page (3). Every target
  URL carries `#sig-slice=<id>` — a fragment is never transmitted (RFC 7230);
  it exists so each capture's recorded `source_uri` names the exact slice
  (keyword/agency/page) that produced it, and the fetch record's per-request
  outcomes are per-slice outcomes. `assert_pulls_subawards` now accepts a
  *declared* prime slice (`kind=usaspending_award_search` + `award_kind=
  prime`); an undeclared prime-only target is still refused.
- `discover()` appends generated targets for `usaspending` (dedupe on id;
  `parameters["sweep_expansion"]=False` is the replay/fixture opt-out) and
  `sam_gov` (dedupe on the decoded `title` param — the P26.4 static
  license-plate-reader target suppresses the generated LPR slice).
- `extract()` routes a usaspending award-search payload (`results`) to
  `procurement_notice` raw records carrying slice provenance; sub-award rows
  additionally emit `subaward` records so the FundingInstrument traceable
  link is preserved. One `usaspending_slice` outcome row per capture
  (items_count + page_metadata) — run-record data, not a claim.
- `_normalize_usaspending_notice()` emits the typed surface: `external_id`,
  `recipient`/`buyer`/`funder` (org candidate identifiers), `amount`,
  `period`, `description`, `federal_award_id`, `notice_type`, `matched_keyword`
  (raw_value = the verbatim literal slice, `evidence.locator` = byte range
  into the named field, `record_row` = the results index), and
  `lifecycle_transition{awarded, action_date}`. Part VIII tokens in emitted
  literals are suppressed at the claim surface. **No deployment predicates
  anywhere** — `deployment_exists`/`device_count`/`camera_count` remain in
  `forbidden_predicate_genres`.
- `fetch()` needed no changes: POST bodies + the `X-Api-Key` header seam
  already ride `PoliteFetcher`; one request per target, counted once, a
  refusal recorded and never re-probed.

### 3. Rights — packet reconciled, no new flip

`usaspending` was already `ingestion_permitted=true` / `CC0-1.0` /

public-domain analysis) and the registry flip were landed in an earlier
phase (recorded on the source row, `last_verified = 2026-09-15`,
GL-GATE-03). P26.14 **re-verified** the packet + row rather than re-flipping

### 4. Fixtures + tests

`tests/connectors/test_procurement.py` +7 tests (46 total): sweep target
generation/bounds, declared-prime vs undeclared-prime refusal, discover
expansion + id dedupe, end-to-end slice → typed claims with locators +
FundingInstrument + no deployment predicates, prime `buyer`-vs-`funder`,
SAM widened targets + title dedupe + no key in URL. `uv run pytest
tests/connectors` 816 passed; `make check` green (3370 tests, verify-gen
clean); `sig-connectors validate` green.

## Hosted run — `sig-ingest-sam-gov` (widened keywords) — **D-FEDERAL.1-1**

- `sig-ingest-sam-gov-6p58k` (12:53Z, on the new image): **failed at the
  1800s task timeout** — no run row (SIGKILL before `store_run_row`; the
  Cloud Run failure IS the recorded outcome).
- Task timeout raised to 3600s on both jobs (the usaspending run's 29.5 min
  was inside the old 30-min wall by 24 seconds); rerun
  `sig-ingest-sam-gov-g92x9` (14:01Z): **failed again at the 3600s wall**
  (~63 min task time).
- **Diagnosis (one keyed probe, key on `X-Api-Key` header, env-scoped,
  never written):** SAM.gov answers **HTTP 429** — verbatim body committed
  at `docs/build/reports/live_runs/2026-09-18_sam_gov_quota_probe.json`:
  `{"code":"900804","message":"Message throttled out","description":"You
  have exceeded your quota .You can access API after 2026-Sep-19 00:00:00
  +0000 UTC"}`. The api.data.gov key's **daily quota** was exhausted by the
  two widened executions (each request's 429 → transport backoff retries →
  minutes per slice → timeout kills). The API's own body names the reset —
  **2026-09-19 00:00 UTC** — so the widened SAM sweep cannot land same-day.
  The refusal is recorded, never bypassed (the D-SOURCES.10-1 OpenStates
  pattern, verbatim quota evidence).
- **Rate-limit honesty note:** the sweep requests each slice exactly once
  per run (one POST/GET per target); the transport's internal 429 backoff
  is the reviewed rate-limit mechanism whose events land in
  `fetch_record.rate_limit_events` on any run that survives to write a
  row. These two executions died before writing — their refusal record is
  the execution failure + the committed 429 probe body. A post-reset run
  is a NEW sweep, not a re-probe of a refused request.
